symptom: TestSnapshotDependents_FindsAssociationsWithoutABaseline (cmd/mxcli/marketplace) failed intermittently: `dependents = []; want MyFirstModule.Config_Account`. Red in CI on main at cd4076243 and on an unrelated PR twice, green at 208a4e6e6; 1 failure in 5 local runs on main. Any read that follows a write within the same second as the previous catalog build answered from the catalog as it was before the write.
file: mdl/catalog/catalog.go ModTimeUnchanged (new) and SetCacheInfo/GetCacheInfo (RFC3339Nano); callers mdl/executor/cmd_catalog.go catalogCurrent and isCacheValid, cmd/mxcli/cmd_describe.go catalogMatchesProject. Tests: mdl/catalog/catalog_test.go, mdl/executor/catalog_freshness_subsecond_test.go, cmd/mxcli/catalog_matches_project_subsecond_test.go, cmd/mxcli/marketplace/snapshot_same_second_test.go
cause: Three freshness checks compared the project file's mtime as whole Unix seconds, and the cache stored it with time.RFC3339 (whole seconds). A write in the same second as the build left the cache looking fresh. The comment justifying it ('handle timezone/precision issues') was about a real worry, but Unix() is already zone independent and an exact Equal on the stored instant has neither problem.
insight: **An intermittent failure whose rate is a fraction of a second over a timing window is a cache key that is too coarse: look for a whole-second timestamp compare before blaming the test or the runner.** Settled by a scratch test that Chtimes the project to a fixed instant, then moves the write +500ms (same second: stale, dependents=0) versus +1500ms (control: seen, dependents=1) - deterministic, where the original test was red 1 run in 6. Three sites compared seconds, not one; grep `.Unix() !=` near MprModTime found all of them. Caches written before the fix hold whole seconds and never equal a fractional mtime, so each project rebuilds once; no wrong answer. Control: reverting ModTimeUnchanged to a seconds compare fails the same-second subtests (marketplace, executor, describe) while the one-second-later control still passes.
